--- freeze: auto title: Unreleased --- # Changelog ::: {#30627877 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pyfixest as pf from pyfixest.report.utils import rename_categoricals df = pf.get_data() fit1 = pf.feols("Y ~ X1", data = df) fit2 = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data = df) fit3 = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data = df) ``` ::: ### Bug Fixes - A multiple estimation call whose expansions mix IV and non-IV models, such as `Y ~ X1 + sw([X2 ~ Z1], Z2)`, raises `FormulaSyntaxError` naming both groups. Before, every model was fitted as IV and the call failed with an unrelated `AttributeError` ([#1809](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1809)). - Several argument errors now say how to fix the call: `vcov="cluster"` points to `vcov={"CRV1": "cluster_var"}`, column names written as `"~f1"` get a hint to drop the tilde, and NW/DK errors show the needed `vcov_kwargs`. A missing `weights` column now raises `ValueError` instead of `AssertionError`, and an unknown `event_study()` estimator raises `ValueError` instead of `NotImplementedError` ([#2041](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2041)). - `vcov()` on a fixed-effects-only fit such as `Y ~ 1 | f1`, or on a multiple estimation that includes one, no longer fails with `AttributeError`. It leaves the fit unchanged, since there are no coefficients to compute a covariance for ([#2054](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2054)). - `FixestMulti.fetch_model()` accepts a model key such as `"Y ~ X1 | f1"`, as documented. Before, it failed with `ValueError: invalid literal for int()`; an unknown key now raises `KeyError` listing the available keys ([#2052](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2052)). ## PyFixest 0.70.0 ### TL;DR - **Varying slopes.** `| f1[X2]` estimates a separate slope on `X2` for each level of `f1`, in `feols()`, `fepois()` and `feglm()`. - **Formulas are parsed by `formulaic`.** The fitted model spec is reused for `predict()` and `fixef()`, so new data is encoded exactly like the estimation data, and `predict(newdata=...)` now works with `i()`, `poly()` and interacted fixed effects. Along with it come new formula spellings: - Fixed-effect interactions are written `f1:f2`. - **New IV syntax.** Instrumental variables are written in brackets, `Y ~ X1 + [X2 ~ Z1]`, which also accepts interacted endogenous terms such as `X2:Z2`. The old `Y ~ X1 | X2 ~ Z1` syntax still works, but it emits a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future release. - **New default demeaner.** LSMR from the `within` package with an adaptive preconditioner. - **Typed results.** Fitted models expose their state as documented components such as `fit.coeftable`, `fit.variance_covariance` and `fit.model`. - **Also new:** anytime-valid inference (SAVI), Word tables from `etable()`, weights and offsets in `feglm()`, clustering on three or more variables, and Python 3.15. - **Many correctness fixes**, several of which change results: `ritest()` p-values, `i()` reference levels, weighted RMSE, the IV first stage, `decompose()` and `quantreg`'s `cfm2` process. See [Bug fixes](#v0700-bug-fixes). - **Before you upgrade:** pyfixest needs Python 3.11+ and newer formulaic and pandas; model names in multiple estimation changed; `fixef()` returns a DataFrame; most private attributes such as `fit._se` are gone; `f1^f2` and `Y ~ X1 | X2 ~ Z1` are deprecated. See [Breaking changes](#v0700-breaking-changes) and [Migrating Fitted-Model Attributes](/how-to/migrate-fit-attributes.qmd). ### New Features {#v0700-new-features} #### Varying Slopes `feols()` (including IV), `fepois()` and `feglm()` accept slopes that vary by fixed-effect level. `f1[X2]` absorbs `f1` and a slope on `X2` for each of its levels; `f1[[X2]]` absorbs only the slopes. Varying slopes need the default `within` demeaner, and `predict()`, `fixef()`, `wildboottest()`, `ritest()`, `decompose()`, `did2s()` and CRV3 or HAC inference don't support them yet ([#1929](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1929), [#1930](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1930), [#1931](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1931), [#1999](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1999)). ::: {#cd3b1287 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1[X2] + f2", data=df).tidy() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Formulas go to `formulaic`, and the fitted `ModelSpec` is reused to build model matrices for `predict()` and `fixef()`. This removes a class of bugs where new data was encoded differently from the estimation data. Most terms now follow `formulaic`'s syntax ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362), [#1437](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1437)). - `predict(newdata=...)` works with `i()`, `poly()` and interacted fixed effects. Unseen levels predict `NaN`. - Fixed-effect interactions are written `f1:f2`. - `sw()`, `csw()`, `sw0()` and `csw0()` accept a single argument, so `| sw0(f1)` fits models with and without `f1` ([#1830](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1830)). The old spellings still work with a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future release. The behaviour changes that come with the new parser are listed under [Breaking changes](#v0700-breaking-changes). #### New IV Syntax Instrumental variables are written as a bracketed block in the main formula, `Y ~ X1 + [X2 ~ Z1]`, combined with fixed effects as `Y ~ X1 + [X2 ~ Z1] | f1` ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362)). The block accepts interacted endogenous terms such as `X2:Z2` ([#1890](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1890)), and the main formula sets the intercept of both stages ([#1998](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1998)). The old `Y ~ X1 | X2 ~ Z1` syntax still works, but it emits a deprecation warning and will be removed in a future release. #### `within` LSMR Is the Default Demeaner The default demeaner is now LSMR from the [`within`](https://github.com/py-econometrics/within) Python package (`within-py`, a new required dependency), replacing the Rust crate compiled into pyfixest. Rust MAP is still available through `MapDemeaner()`. The default `preconditioner="auto"` now selects `within`'s adaptive preconditioner. It starts with a cheap diagonal preconditioner and builds additive Schwarz only when convergence stalls, which skips Schwarz's setup cost on well-connected fixed effects where it rarely pays off. `fepois()` and `feglm()` still reuse the preconditioner across IRLS iterations ([#1920](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1920), [#1922](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1922), [#1923](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1923)). #### Typed Fitted-Model State Fitted models expose what they computed as documented components instead of private attributes ([#1533](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1533), [#2028](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2028)): | Component | Contents | |---|---| | `fit.model` | formula, dependent variable, fixed effects, estimator, sample split | | `fit.options` | estimation options: `ssc`, weights, demeaner, storage settings | | `fit.sample_info` | number of observations and dropped rows by reason | | `fit.coeftable` | estimates, standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals | | `fit.variance_covariance` | covariance matrix, small-sample corrections, cluster counts | | `fit.sandwich` | scores, Hessian and bread | | `fit.fitstat` | RMSE, R² measures, deviance, log-likelihoods | | `fit.fitted_values` | in-sample predictions on the link and response scale | | `fit.collinearity` | columns dropped as collinear | | `fit.fixef_counts`, `fit.fixef_estimates` | fixed-effect level counts; fixed-effect estimates after `fixef()` | | `fit.first_stage` | IV first stage and its diagnostics | | `fit.wald` | joint Wald test from fitting, replaced by each `wald_test()` call | | `fit.capabilities` | inference and post-estimation methods the model supports | | `fit.solution` | quantile-regression solver state | The components that describe the model and its sample survive `store_data=False` and `lean=True`. #### Safe Anytime-Valid Inference (SAVI) `evalue()`, `pvalue_savi()` and `confint(inference_type="savi")` return e-values, sequential p-values and confidence sequences for linear regression, following [Lindon et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2026.2692052) ([#1386](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1386)). ::: {#cffd7236 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=df, vcov="iid") fit.confint(inference_type="savi") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: #### Smaller Additions - `etable(type="docx")` returns or saves editable Word tables, styled through `docx_style` ([#1541](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1541)). - `feglm()` accepts `weights`, `weights_type`, `offset` and `family="poisson"`. Offsets can be expressions such as `offset="log(exposure)"` ([#1349](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1349), [#1458](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1458)). - `fepois()` converges faster thanks to step-halving and warm starts ([#1347](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1347)). - Cluster-robust inference accepts three or more cluster variables, e.g. `vcov={"CRV1": "firm + year + region"}` ([#1599](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1599)). - `tidy()`, `confint()` and `summary()` gain an `inference_type` argument. `confint(inference_type="simult")` replaces `confint(joint=True)` ([#1398](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1398)). - Python 3.15 is supported. On 3.15, plots use matplotlib because `lets-plot` has no compatible release yet ([#2030](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2030)). ### Breaking Changes {#v0700-breaking-changes} #### Requirements - Python 3.11 or newer ([#2029](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2029)). - `formulaic>=1.2.2,<1.3`, `pandas>=2.3.3`, `narwhals>=1.17` and the new `within-py>=0.4,<0.5` ([#1895](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1895), [#1946](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1946), [#1954](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1954), [#1920](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1920)). #### Formulas and Model Names - Model names in multiple estimation are canonical formulas. `"Y ~ sw(X2+X1, X1)"` now names its models `"Y ~ 1 + X2 + X1"` and `"Y ~ 1 + X1"`. Update `rename_models` mappings and lookups into `all_fitted_models`. Expansions that produce the same model twice estimate it once and warn ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362), [#1873](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1873), [#1890](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1890)). - `fixef()` returns a DataFrame with columns `variable`, `code`, `level` and `coefficient` instead of a nested dict. With two or more fixed effects, the reference levels of the second and later ones are listed with coefficient 0 ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362)). - The main formula sets the intercept for both IV stages; a `0` or `1` inside the IV block is ignored ([#1998](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1998)). - Fixed effects must be data columns, or `:` interactions of them, whose names are valid Python identifiers. Transforms and `object`-dtype columns are rejected, and `predict()` requires the same dtype as at fit time ([#1898](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1898), [#1902](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1902)). - `log()` in formulas is now `np.log`. Zeros are counted as infinite rather than missing, and numpy warns on zero or negative inputs. Estimates are unchanged ([#1806](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1806), [#1869](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1869)). - Some malformed formulas raise `formulaic.errors.FormulaSyntaxError`, which is unrelated to `pyfixest.errors.FormulaSyntaxError`; catch both ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362)). - `factor_interaction` moved to `pyfixest.estimation.formula.transforms.factor_interaction` ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362)). #### Fitted Models and Post-Estimation - Most private attributes from 0.60 are removed. Accessing one, e.g. `fit._se`, raises an `AttributeError` that points to the migration guide; use `fit.coeftable.se` instead. Names used by released versions of marginaleffects and maketables keep working, and the IV attributes `_model_1st_stage`, `_f_stat_1st_stage` and `_eff_F` keep working with a deprecation warning. See [Migrating Fitted-Model Attributes](/how-to/migrate-fit-attributes.qmd) ([#2028](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2028)). - `pf.ssc()` returns a frozen `Ssc` instead of a dict (dicts are still accepted as input). `pf.get_ssc()` takes an `Ssc` and `DegreesOfFreedomCounts` and returns a `SmallSampleCorrection`. `wald_test()` returns a `WaldTest` instead of a Series ([#1595](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1595), [#1591](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1591)). - `feglm().resid()` returns response residuals `y - mu` by default; the old working residuals are `resid(type="working")` ([#1349](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1349)). - `feglm(family="gaussian")` now reproduces `feols()` exactly, including its small-sample correction ([#1352](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1352)). - Passing `data` to `vcov()` raises `ValueError`. It silently misaligned rows in cluster-robust standard errors ([#1825](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1825), [#1956](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1956)). - `vcov` and `vcov_kwargs` are checked before fitting, so a misspelled estimator or a missing cluster column fails early with `ValueError` ([#1577](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1577)). - Several methods that ran on unsupported models and returned wrong numbers now raise: `ccv()` on weighted models; `Feols.update()` with `inplace=True`, weights or IV; CRV3 on non-Poisson GLMs; `ritest()` on models other than OLS and Poisson; `wildboottest()` on IV and non-OLS models; `decompose()` on non-`feols` models or with multiway clustering; `predict()`, `wildboottest()`, `ccv()`, `decompose()` and `vcov()` updates on `did2s()` fits; and `predict(se_fit=True)` for GLMs and quantile regression ([#1516](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1516), [#1620](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1620), [#1726](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1726), [#1698](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1698), [#1652](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1652), [#1983](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1983)). - Invalid arguments to `ccv()`, `ritest()`, `event_study()`, `did2s()` and `lpdid()` raise `ValueError` or `TypeError` instead of `AssertionError`. Every warning now has an explicit category and points at your code rather than pyfixest internals ([#1723](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1723)). - Methods that need data removed by `store_data=False` or `lean=True` raise `MissingModelDataError` ([#1540](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1540)). - pyfixest no longer uses or reseeds NumPy's global random generator. Data from `get_blw()`, `get_sharkfin()` and `get_panel_dgp_stagg()` changes, and `ccv()` and simultaneous confidence intervals need `seed=` to be reproducible ([#1705](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1705)). - The model classes take `options=` and `sample_split=` constructor arguments instead of many loose keyword arguments ([#1598](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1598), [#1719](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1719)). - `did2s()` rejects a second stage without an intercept, IV formulas and multiple estimation ([#1918](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1918)). #### Demeaner - `preconditioner="auto"` now means adaptive, so results can differ slightly from 0.60. Pass `preconditioner="additive"` for the old behaviour ([#1922](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1922)). - `pf.Preconditioner` is `within.Preconditioner`. Its `variant` is replaced by `config`, and `build_time_seconds` is renamed `build_duration_seconds`. Preconditioners pickled with older versions can't be loaded ([#1920](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1920)). #### Deprecated These still work and emit a warning ([#1362](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1362), [#1437](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1437), [#1398](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1398), [#1704](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1704), [#2028](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/2028)): - `Y ~ X1 | f1^f2`: write `Y ~ X1 | f1:f2`. - `Y ~ X1 | X2 ~ Z1`: write `Y ~ X1 + [X2 ~ Z1]`. - `Y + Y2 ~ X1`: write `sw(Y, Y2) ~ X1`. - `confint(joint=True)`: use `confint(inference_type="simult")`. - `FixestMulti.FixestFormulaDict`: use `fit.model.parsed_formula`. - `fit.get_performance()`: use `fit.fitstat`. - `fit.n_separation_na`: use `fit.sample_info`. - `maxiter`, `tol` and `separation_check` on GLM fits: use `fit.options`. #### Removed - The `demeaner_backend`, `fixef_tol` and `fixef_maxiter` arguments; use the `Demeaner` API from 0.60 ([#1332](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1332)). - The JAX demeaner and solver, and the SciPy and CuPy LSMR backends. On GPU, use `LsmrDemeaner(backend="torch", device="cuda")` ([#1333](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1333), [#1334](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1334), [#1718](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1718)). - `FeolsCompressed` ([#1336](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1336)) and `pf.dtable()`; use `maketables.DTable()` instead ([#1404](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1404)). - The `fit.FixestFormula` attribute (use `fit.model`) and the callable `Feiv.first_stage()`; `fit.first_stage` is now a component ([#1610](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1610), [#1588](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1588)). - `FixestFormulaParser`, `model_matrix_fixest()`, the `pyfixest.estimation.feols_`, `feiv_` and `fepois_` modules (import `Feols`, `Feiv` and `Fepois` from `pyfixest.estimation` instead), and several unused helpers in `pyfixest.utils` ([#1607](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1607), [#1704](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1704)). ### Bug Fixes {#v0700-bug-fixes} #### Inference - `ritest()` now permutes the observed treatment. It used to draw treatments uniformly from the distinct values, which changed the share treated and typically made p-values too small. This also affects `rwolf()` and `wyoung()` with `sampling_method="ri"`. With `cluster=`, a treatment that varies within a cluster raises `ValueError` ([#1964](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1964), [#1965](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1965)). - `ritest(type="randomization-t")`, `ritest(cluster=...)` and `ccv()` keep the fitted model's covariance estimator and small-sample corrections, and the randomization t-statistic is centred at the null ([#1986](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1986)–[#1989](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1989)). - `ritest()` rebuilds treatment-dependent interactions on every draw ([#1979](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1979)), and its fast algorithm works with interacted fixed effects ([#1780](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1780), [#1866](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1866)). - `vcov({"CRV3": ...})`, `ritest()` and `ccv()` refit with all the original estimation options. Before, a Poisson `offset` and options such as `context` or `drop_intercept` were dropped ([#1709](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1709), [#1711](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1711)). - CRV3 on `event_study()` fits refits with `feols()` instead of Poisson ([#1619](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1619)). - `wildboottest()` and `decompose()` leave out covariates that the fit dropped as collinear ([#1778](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1778), [#1867](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1867)), and `wildboottest()` requires `param` instead of returning p = 0 ([#1959](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1959), [#1969](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1969)). - `confint()` with `keep` or `drop` could attach intervals to the wrong coefficients ([#1397](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1397)). - The RMSE of weighted fits divides by the sum of weights ([#1883](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1883), [#1884](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1884)). #### IV - The first stage uses the second stage's sample, options and full covariance estimator. Before, two-way clustering fell back to one-way clustering, and `vcov="NW"` or `"DK"` failed ([#1710](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1710)). - Redundant instruments no longer change the first-stage F or effective F ([#1996](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1996)). Instruments that don't identify an endogenous variable raise `IVIdentificationError` ([#1891](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1891), [#1992](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1992), [#1993](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1993)). - Covariates named like generated values (`X2_hat`), misplaced IV blocks, and `|` inside IV expressions are handled correctly ([#1736](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1736), [#1766](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1766), [#1890](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1890), [#1834](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1834)). #### Formulas - Multiple estimation no longer reuses demeaned values from a different expression that happens to have the same column name ([#1762](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1762), [#1914](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1914)). - `i()` fixes: - a boolean second variable fits one slope per level ([#1756](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1756), [#1907](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1907)); - levels come from the data before missing rows are dropped, and unused categories of a `Categorical` are ignored, which fixes the reference level in some models ([#1769](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1769), [#1912](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1912)); - without an intercept, every interaction cell is kept ([#1767](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1767), [#1942](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1942)); - `C(k)` marks a numeric second variable as a factor, so `i(a, C(k))` interacts two factors instead of fitting slopes. `ref2` and `bin2` no longer turn a numeric second variable into a factor and raise instead ([#1770](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1770), [#1804](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1804), [#1943](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1943)); - `bin` is validated ([#1771](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1771), [#1945](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1945)); - factor-by-factor interactions work with NumPy 1.25 ([#1909](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1909), [#1952](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1952)). - Formulas whose terms produce duplicate column names raise instead of keeping only the last column ([#1928](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1928), [#1947](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1947)). - `sw()` and friends work across several lines and with a space before the parenthesis ([#1810](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1810), [#1847](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1847)). Stepwise terms keep their grouping under `:`, `*` and `-` ([#1828](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1828)). - `log()` accepts nullable `Float64` and `Int64` columns ([#1807](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1807), [#1829](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1829)). - `weights=` accepts column names with spaces or operators ([#1815](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1815), [#1844](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1844)). the other backends run in a separate workflow ([#1485](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1485)). - Repository-local skills and developer guides for contributors and coding agents ([#1476](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1476)). - `pixi.lock` uses the v7 format, which needs pixi 0.71.0 or newer ([#1498](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1498)). - Internals: fitted models keep the formula `ModelMatrix`, the demeaning cache hands out read-only `float64` arrays, and weighting happens inside the solver instead of on stored arrays ([#1499](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1499), [#1516](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1516), [#1520](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/pull/1520)). ## PyFixest 0.60.0 This release focuses on the fixed-effects demeaning stack. The main changes are a typed demeaner API, switching from `numba` to Rust for the default MAP demeaning algorithm, reusable `within` preconditioners, PyTorch-backed LSMR demeaning on CPU and GPU, and a few deprecations for older backend options. It also adds `fepois()` offsets, Typst output for `etable()`, and several `panelview()` fixes. ### Rust MAP Default and Optional Numba `MapDemeaner()` now defaults to `backend="rust"`. The Numba MAP backend remains available via `MapDemeaner(backend="numba")`, and the fast randomization-inference path (`fit.ritest(..., choose_algorithm="fast")`) still uses Numba. Numba is now an optional dependency installed with `pip install pyfixest[numba]`. ### Typed Demeaner API A new typed demeaner API replaces the old `demeaner_backend`, `fixef_tol`, and `fixef_maxiter` arguments to `feols()`, `fepois()`, and related functions. Instead of passing a set of loosely related keyword arguments, you can now pass a configuration object that makes the chosen algorithm, tolerance, iteration limit, and device explicit. ```python import pyfixest as pf from pyfixest.demeaners import MapDemeaner, LsmrDemeaner # Old API (deprecated) fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=df, demeaner_backend="rust", fixef_tol=1e-8, fixef_maxiter=5000) # New API fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=df, demeaner=MapDemeaner(backend="rust", fixef_tol=1e-8, fixef_maxiter=5000)) fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=df, demeaner=LsmrDemeaner(backend="within", fixef_atol=1e-8, fixef_btol=1e-8, fixef_maxiter=5000)) fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1", data=df, demeaner=LsmrDemeaner(backend="torch", device="cuda")) ``` **Deprecations:** The `demeaner_backend`, `fixef_tol`, and `fixef_maxiter` arguments to `feols()` and related functions are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. The `_fixef_tol` and `_fixef_maxiter` attributes on fitted model objects are removed; going forward, this information is collected from the typed `fit.options.demeaner` via `fit.options.demeaner.fixef_tol` and `fit.options.demeaner.fixef_maxiter`. **Default change:** `LsmrDemeaner()` now defaults to `fixef_maxiter=1_000` (previously inherited `10_000` from `BaseDemeaner`). LSMR typically converges in far fewer than 1,000 iterations, but if you hit `"Demeaning failed after 1000 iterations"` on a difficult problem, pass `LsmrDemeaner(fixef_maxiter=10_000)` (or higher) explicitly. The lower-level `pyfixest.core.demean.demean_within(...)` helper also tightened its default `tol` from `1e-6` to `1e-8`. Calls through `LsmrDemeaner` already pass `max(fixef_atol, fixef_btol)` (default `1e-8`), so the new default matches what the typed API was already using. Only direct callers of `demean_within(...)` with no `tol` argument see a behaviour change. ### Diagonal Preconditioner for the `within` LSMR Backend PyFixest now bundles version 0.2.0 of the `within` Rust solver, which adds a diagonal (Jacobi) preconditioner. You can use it with `LsmrDemeaner(backend="within", preconditioner="diagonal")`, alongside the existing `"additive"` (default) and `"off"` options. ### Reusing Preconditioners The `within` LSMR backend now exposes its additive Schwarz preconditioner so the (potentially) expensive setup phase can be amortised when users explicitly reuse it across regressions based on the same fixed-effect design. ```python import pyfixest as pf from pyfixest.demeaners import LsmrDemeaner df = pf.get_data() # Every Feols-family fit exposes the preconditioner that was used. fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 | f1 + f2", data=df, demeaner=LsmrDemeaner()) pre = fit.preconditioner # Pass it back via `LsmrDemeaner(preconditioner=...)` to skip the setup # phase on a later fit over the same design. fit_fast = pf.feols( "Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=df, demeaner=LsmrDemeaner(preconditioner=pre), ) ``` For `fepois()` and `feglm()`, the first IWLS iteration builds the preconditioner and every subsequent iteration reuses it under the changing working weights. That means the reused preconditioner is "stale" because it was built under the initial iteration's weights. LSMR still converges to the correct demeaned values, but it may take a few extra iterations per IWLS step. The setup phase is paid once instead of once per IWLS iteration. Each `Preconditioner` also reports its original setup time via `preconditioner.build_time_seconds`, which can be useful when profiling large fixed-effect problems. `Preconditioner` instances are pickleable, so the setup phase can also be amortised across Python sessions. See [Choosing a Demeaner Backend](how-to/demeaner-backends.qmd) for details. ### PyTorch LSMR Backend PyFixest now includes an experimental PyTorch-backed LSMR demeaner. It supports CPU execution, CUDA GPUs, and Apple Silicon MPS: ```python fit = pf.feols( "Y ~ X1 | f1 + f2", data=df, demeaner=pf.LsmrDemeaner(backend="torch", device="cuda"), ) ``` Install the optional dependency with `pip install pyfixest[torch]`. For CUDA, you may need to install a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build separately, following the PyTorch installation instructions. ### JAX, CuPy, and SciPy Backend Deprecations The `jax` MAP demeaner backend, the `cupy` / `scipy` LSMR demeaner backends, and the `solver="jax"` OLS solver option are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Passing any of them now raises a `DeprecationWarning`. We recommend the following replacements: - **JAX MAP on CPU** → `MapDemeaner()` (the default rust MAP). - **JAX MAP on GPU** or **`LsmrDemeaner(backend="cupy", device="cuda")`** → `LsmrDemeaner(backend="torch", device="cuda")`. - **Scipy or Cupy LSMR on CPU** → `LsmrDemeaner()` (the default `within` backend). ### Regression Compression Deprecation The `use_compression` argument to `feols()` is deprecated and no longer supported. This feature implemented the in-memory regression compression approach from [Wong et al. (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.11297) via a Mundlak/sufficient-statistics transform, and the implementation has now been removed. For large-dataset use cases, the [`duckreg`](https://github.com/py-econometrics/duckreg) package provides a more general out-of-memory solution. See [#1302](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1302) for context. Passing `use_compression=True` now raises a `NotImplementedError`. ### Offsets in `fepois()` `pf.fepois()` now supports offsets via the new `offset` argument. This is useful for Poisson models with an exposure term, such as `offset="log_population"`. Thanks to @bradhackinen and @marie-gar for the contribution. ### `etable()` Typst Output and Formatting `pf.etable()` now supports `type="typst"` output. Its default `coef_fmt` is also inherited from `maketables`, which keeps PyFixest closer to the table engine it uses internally. As before, significance stars are controlled by the coefficient format string: include `*` on a statistic token, for example `b:.3f*`, when you want stars in the rendered table. ### panelview Bug Fixes - Validates that the `treat` column is binary (`{0, 1, True, False}`) and normalizes it to boolean before plotting, matching R's `panelView` behavior. See [#1311](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1311). - Fixes `sort_by_timing` to sort units by the period of first treatment (via `argmax`) rather than by the total number of treated periods. - Raises an explicit `ValueError` when the `treat` column contains missing values instead of silently dropping them. - Fixes a latent bug in `_plot_panelview` where passing a user-supplied `ax` together with `legend=True` referenced an unbound figure variable; the colorbar is now attached via `ax.figure`. ## PyFixest 0.50.1 ### Bug Fixes - Fixes an import-time failure on Python 3.13 in some environments where a `narwhals` typing alias was exposed as a string at runtime. This could cause imports of `feols()` / `feglm()` to fail before any model code ran. See [#1263](https://github.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/issues/1263) for details. - Clarifies `pf.etable()` significance-star behavior after the migration to `maketables`: stars are rendered only when `coef_fmt` includes `*` on a statistic token, for example `b*` or `b:.3f*`. ## PyFixest 0.50.0 ::: {.callout-tip} You can install the latest pre-release to try out the new features: ```{.bash .code-copy} pip install pyfixest==0.50.0a2 pip install --pre pyfixest ``` ::: ### New Demeaner Backend via the `within` package We recently came together for a PyFixest sprint with the team from AppliedAI, and one new feature that already made it's way into the code base is a new typed demeaner configuration that performs really well for sparse fixed effects structures. The new solver is exposed via `pf.LsmrDemeaner(backend="within")` and is a significant performance improvement for sparse fixed effects structures - such as matched employer-employee data, patient-doctor panels, or trade networks - where the standard MAP algorithm might struggle. On well-connected graphs, `pf.MapDemeaner(backend="rust")` remains competitive, but on sparse graphs the within-based solver is dramatically faster. ![](explanation/figures/base-benchmarks/bench_difficult.png){width=85% fig-align="center"} *Benchmark on a sparse fixed effects structure: vanilla MAP degrades dramatically, while `within` LSMR via `pf.LsmrDemeaner()` remains fast.* For a detailed explanation of why some fixed effects problems are harder than others and comprehensive benchmarks, see [When Are Fixed Effects Estimations Difficult?](explanation/difficult-fixed-effects.md). Special shoutout to [Kristof](https://github.com/schroedk) from the [appliedAI Institute](https://www.appliedai-institute.de/en/) who developed and implemented the new algorithm. ### Reworked Formula Parsing and New `i()` Operator The formula parsing module has been significantly reworked. The new implementation introduces a cleaner `Formula` class, a rewritten `i()` operator that closely follows R's `fixest` syntax, and new multiple estimation operators. #### New `i()` operator The `i()` operator now follows the `fixest` naming convention, using `::` to separate variable names from levels. The API remains unchanged for backward compatibility. - Because the function is not at the core of `pyixest` functionality, we will deprecate `pf.dtable()`. A `FutureWarning` is now emitted. The function has been moved to `maketables` and can be used by calling `maketables.DTable()` directly. - The same applies for `pf.make_table()`, which has been an internal utility function to create tables. ``` ::: ::: ## PyFixest 0.40.1 ### Breaking Changes for compatibility with `fixest` 0.13 `fixest` 0.13 has recently been released to CRAN, with a range of breaking changes. We are following these in pyfixet 0.40.0. - The default inference method is now always "iid". Before, both `fixest` and `pyfixest` would default to cluster by the first fixest effect in the presence of fixed effect. - The arguments of the `pf.ssc()` functions have been renamed: `adj` becomes `k_adj`, `fixef_k` becomes `k_fixef`, `cluster_df` becomes `G_df`, and `cluster_adj` becomes `G_adj`. Backwards compatibility is ensured. - `fixest` no longer applies the `G/(G-1)` small sample correction for heteroskedastic errors. The argument is now only relevant for cluster robust errors. - If the `k_adj` arg is set to `True` with heteroskedastic errors, the applied small sample correction now is `N / (N-k)` and no longer `(N-1) / (N-df_k)`, as was previously the case and is still the case for iid and cluster robust errors. - The `k_fixef` option `"nested"` has been renamed to `"nonnested"`. - The `fixef_rm` argument is changed from default `"none"` to `"singleton"` for all estimation functions. This has no impact on point estimates, but might change inference due to a smaller number of observations in the degree of freedom correction. - The multicollinearity default tolerance has been reduced from 1e-10 to 1e-09. - The attribute `_dof_k` has been renamed to `_df_k`. Other related changes: - The arguments to adjust the small samples for the `wildboottest` methods have been renamed to `k_adj` and `G_adj`. ### Moved to `pixi.toml` and install from conda-forge We have been using pixi as our package manager for a while and are moving from a `pyproject.toml` to using a `pixi.toml` for specifying dependencies. We also install all package by default from the free and open source conda-forge. Because of some environment resolution challenges around an old version of `rpy2`that we need for testing `pyfixest` against `fixest`, we temporarily have dropped support for the dev and docs environments for windows. A fix is work in progress. ## New Features ### CuPy and SciPy Backends via LSMR We add CuPy and SciPy Backend to run the demeaning algorithm on the GPU via the sparse LSMR solver. For problems where the standard demeaner struggles to converge, this strategy can lead to significant speedups if paired with a GPU. ![Complex Fixed Effects Benchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/py-econometrics/pyfixest/master/benchmarks/complex_benchmarks.png) ### HAC Standard Errors We now support HAC standard errors!
